novel_mechanics_found: sp80 is a spill-routing puzzle whose flow physics I fully decoded this session. (1) FLOW DIRECTION alternates per level: L3 towers shoot vines UPWARD into arch-hole targets; L4 flips to a ceiling spout pouring DOWNWARD into U-cups; L5 is upward again. (2) SPLITTER BARS: a stream hitting a bar runs along its far side to both ends and re-emits 3px branch streams just outside each end; streams merge when feeding the same bar. (3) WALL MATERIALS: the blue border/ceiling band AND the grey floor are lethal - any stream terminating on them fails the commit, so every stream must end inside a target; branches pushed off the board edge in L3 vanish harmlessly (the only safe disposal). (4) VERTICAL CLEARANCE (the subtle killer): a bar's run occupies the 3 pixel-rows on its far side, so a bar placed exactly one cell beyond another bar's face BLOCKS that bar's run from spreading - silently deleting its branch outputs (cost me a failed commit in L4). (5) EMBEDDED SOURCES: L4's long bar carries a 3px source segment that drips its own stream wherever the bar is moved - a movable second spout that the winning layout uses to feed a cup directly. (6) Pieces move on per-piece 3px sub-lattices with positional caps (L3 bars cannot rise above grid-row 4). (7) L5 introduces a NEW selectable L-shaped piece (color 15) with an invisible movement boundary (cannot cross left of x=14), plus a wall-sculpture with a 3px side-facing notch; routing all three holes cleanly was NOT sufficient to win L5, so this piece carries an undiscovered win condition.
narrative: Replayed the 33-action banked prefix to verified level 2. Solved LEVEL 3 (win at step 100) by inducing the upward-flow/splitter physics from one throwaway commit, deriving that ceiling contact fails but off-board branches vanish, then routing all three tower vines into the three arch holes with a 4-bar cascade. Solved LEVEL 4 (win at step 195) after discovering the embedded-source segment, remeasuring the cup lattice, designing a zero-stray two-source cascade, and fixing a final vertical-clearance collision. Ran the reproduction gate on the exact 195-action live line: reached_level=4, reproduced=True. Spent the remaining budget on LEVEL 5: routed both tower vines into all three arch holes with zero strays (verified in the spill animation), but the commit still failed - the new L-shaped color-15 piece evidently carries an extra win condition. Tested the socket theory (the wall sculpture has a matching 3px notch) but the piece is hard-blocked at an invisible x=14 boundary and cannot reach it. Stopped at 445/500 steps with L3+L4 verified.
gotchas: ACTION6 click selects a piece (selected renders color 9, idle 8); ACTION1-4 move it (up/down/left/right, no rotation observed in L3-L5); ACTION5 commits the spill. Failed commits are cheap: the spill animates, drains, and pieces keep their positions.
Commit attempts appear to be a limited resource: black pixels accumulate on a border row per commit (bottom row in L3, top row in L4), resetting each level.
Streams are 3px wide and live on per-piece 3px sub-lattices - measure piece and target positions programmatically from the frame; off-by-one eyeballing wastes commits.

Blue (color 1) band/border contact = fail; grey (color 14/E) floor contact = fail; cup/arch masonry (color 11) top-landings pool and partially fill cups but the outside spill then hits the floor, so pooling cannot appear in a winning layout.
L3: bars cannot move above grid row 4 (movement cap). Edge-vines (towers at columns 1 and 14 of 16) force branches at columns <=0 / >=15: push them OFF-BOARD (safe vanish), never into the ceiling.
Vertical clearance rule: leave at least 2 cell-rows between a bar's face and any bar it feeds, or the run cannot spread and its outputs silently vanish.

L4's 21px bar has an embedded 3px source at offset +9 from its left end - position the BAR so the drip lands where you need a free stream (winning layout: bar at [32,52] row 17 - outputs feed cups 2 and 4, drip feeds cup 3, while a 12px bar at [20,31] row 11 splits the spout and a 15px bar at [14,28] row 17 feeds cups 1 and 2).

L5 (unsolved): moving the 9px bar to [41,49]@47 splits the right vine into holes 2+3 and clearing the left vine's column feeds hole 1 - all three holes verified fed with zero strays, and the level still does NOT complete. The L-shaped color-15 piece is selectable and movable but hard-blocked at x>=14; the left wall-sculpture has a 3px notch at rows 38-40, cols 8-10 (side-facing, unreachable by streams and unreachable by the piece) - the win condition tied to these two objects is still undiscovered. Next ideas: check whether the F-piece must be positioned somewhere specific on the right side, whether a stream must TOUCH the F-piece, or whether the F-piece must ride a bar.
